top_story.headline: Khanna and Massie file bipartisan war powers resolution on Houthi hostilities in Yemen
top_story.dek: The concurrent resolution would direct the President to remove U.S. armed forces from unauthorized hostilities against the Houthis.
paragraphs: On Friday, October 9, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) introduced H. Con. Res. 124, which invokes section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to direct the President to remove United States armed forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized. The Congressional Record lists Rep. Thomas Massie as the co-lead alongside Khanna, making it a cross-party effort.

The resolution was referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs. It is one of 31 bills and resolutions introduced in the House on a day when both chambers met only briefly: the Senate held a pro forma session lasting 38 seconds, and the House adjourned at 12:32 p.m. until Tuesday.

sections.headline: Brief House and Senate sessions; 31 measures introduced
paragraphs: The Senate met at 1:30:01 p.m. in pro forma session and adjourned at 1:30:39 p.m. until 3:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The House adjourned at 12:32 p.m. until 1:30 p.m. the same day, and the House Speaker, Mike Johnson, appointed Rep. Erin Houchin to act as Speaker pro tempore to sign enrolled bills and joint resolutions through the remainder of the 119th Congress.

Beyond the Khanna–Massie war powers measure, other introductions include H.R. 10768 on artificial intelligence threats, H.R. 10772 on Ukrainian defense technologies, and H. Res. 1622 backing Christopher Columbus monuments. The full list follows; all 31 were introduced October 9, 2026.

items: H.R. 10768, sponsored by Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI-7) — Would create an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10769, sponsored by Rep. Everton Blair (D-GA-13) — Would allow certain facilities within the right-of-way of any federal-aid highway; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
H.R. 10770, sponsored by Rep. Robert P. Bresnahan (R-PA-8) — Would temporarily limit the use of rebates under the 340B drug discount program; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10771, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — Would create an emergency preparedness grant program for higher education institutions; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
H.R. 10772, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA-21) — Would evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10773, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Crank (R-CO-5) — Would amend the Internal Revenue Code to prevent governmental interference in the operation of private and religious schools; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10774, sponsored by Rep. Suzan K. DelBene (D-WA-1) — Would prohibit the taking, importation, exportation and breeding of certain cetaceans for public display by amending the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 and the Animal Welfare Act; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources and, in addition, the Committee on Agriculture.

H.R. 10775, sponsored by Rep. Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA-10) — Would direct the Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission to set up a task force studying the effects of automated accounts on social media, public discourse and elections; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10776, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — Would change requirements on allowed take of marine mammals under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10777, sponsored by Rep. Pat Fallon (R-TX-4) — Would codify certain policies to combat transnational cyber-enabled crime; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, with the Committees on Homeland Security and Foreign Affairs in addition.

H.R. 10778, sponsored by Rep. Valerie P. Foushee (D-NC-4) — Would create a tax credit for health care facilities that use certain low-emission anesthetic gases; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10779, sponsored by Rep. Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY-2) — Would name the Postal Service facility at 1905 Route 112 in Medford, New York, the “Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos Post Office Building”; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10780, sponsored by Rep. Jared F. Golden (D-ME-2) — Would modify and enhance the federal budgeting and appropriations process; referred to the Committee on Rules, with the Committees on the Budget, House Administration, Appropriations, and Oversight and Government Reform in addition.

H.R. 10781, sponsored by Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-8) — Would request that the President designate a month each year as “National American History and Founders Month”; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
H.R. 10782, sponsored by Rep. Jahana Hayes (D-CT-5) — Would reauthorize the Clean School Bus Program; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10783, sponsored by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC-1) — Would provide for payment of attorney’s fees to a prevailing defendant in a civil action for defamation or libel; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10784, sponsored by Rep. Richard McCormick (R-GA-7) — Would amend the Internal Revenue Code to provide home ownership assistance; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, with the Committee on Financial Services in addition.
H.R. 10785, sponsored by Rep. Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11) — Would reauthorize the SCORE small-business mentoring program under the Small Business Act; referred to the Committee on Small Business.

H.R. 10786, sponsored by Rep. Max L. Miller (R-OH-7) — Would require certain colleges to make U.S.-citizen students pass the United States naturalization test in order to graduate; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10787, sponsored by Rep. Gregory F. Murphy (R-NC-3) — Would exclude urological and ostomy supplies from Medicare competitive acquisition programs for five years; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, with the Committee on Ways and Means in addition.

H.R. 10788, sponsored by Rep. Frank Pallone (D-NJ-6) — Short title: Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act. Would adjust the surprise medical billing requirements for private health insurance; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, with the Committees on Education and Workforce and Ways and Means in addition.

H.R. 10789, sponsored by Rep. Jimmy Patronis (R-FL-1) — Would establish a moratorium on oil and gas production and exploration in the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10790, sponsored by Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-WA-3) — Would require that at least one member of the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board have demonstrated knowledge and substantial experience in the trades or industrial labor; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10791, sponsored by Rep. Michael A. Rulli (R-OH-6) — Would bar federal funds to any state or local government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10792, sponsored by Rep. Janice D. Schakowsky (D-IL-9) — Would provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the authority of the Federal Trade Commission; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, with the Committee on Energy and Commerce in addition.

H.R. 10793, sponsored by Rep. Derek Schmidt (R-KS-2) — Would modify Department of Defense authority for installation support services and intergovernmental support agreements; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10794, sponsored by Rep. Norma J. Torres (D-CA-35) — Would create a grant program to help states improve access to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC); referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H. Con. Res. 124, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — Would direct the President, under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized; co-led with Rep. Thomas Massie; referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.
H. Res. 1621, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA-46) — Expresses profound sorrow over the death of Alexander Michel Odeh; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H. Res. 1622, sponsored by Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24) — Expresses support for preserving, protecting and maintaining statues and monuments honoring Christopher Columbus; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H. Res. 1623, sponsored by Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4) — Expresses support for recognizing October 2026 as “National Dyslexia Awareness Month”; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
